concepts.title: Reading Large Numbers: Lakh and Crore
concepts.definition: Large numbers are read through place value in the Indian system: ten thousands make a lakh, a hundred lakh make a crore, and commas group digits to make a number like 1,52,700 readable at a glance.
concepts.key_idea: Place value is the address system of digits: the same digit changes value a hundredfold when it moves two places left.
question_patterns: how many zeros does a lakh have
read the number 152700 in the indian system
how many lakhs make a crore
write the number that has 3 lakhs 2 thousands and 5 ones

concepts.title: Multiplying and Adding Large Quantities
concepts.definition: Real situations multiply into large numbers quickly: boxes of pencils, sacks of rice or visitors in a month; multiplying the group size by the number of groups gives totals that run into lakhs and crores.
concepts.key_idea: Large totals are built from small factors: multiply group size by group count and check the place value of the answer.

concepts.title: Estimation and Approximation
concepts.definition: Exact answers are not always needed: rounding numbers to the nearest thousand or lakh gives quick estimates, and estimating before calculating gives a check on the final answer.
concepts.key_idea: Estimates trade accuracy for speed: round first, calculate, and the estimate guards against silly mistakes.

concepts.title: Comparing and Expanding Large Numbers
concepts.definition: To compare large numbers, count digits first and then compare places from the left; to expand a number means to write it as the sum of the place values of its digits.
concepts.key_idea: Left to right is the law of comparison: the first place where two digits differ decides the bigger number.
